summary: The scan-based rewrite of trimLiterals is behaviorally equivalent to the old regex in every case I could construct: exhaustive differential testing over all strings up to length 8 on {a, space, quote, double-quote, tab} (488,280 cases), 400k random longer cases, and 300 large quote-dense cases all produced zero differences, including the subtle backtracking case where an unclosed literal's match ends at the last '' pair and scanning resumes at the pair's second quote. The 15MB acceptance input completes in ~14ms with the exact expected output (the old regex demonstrably throws RangeError on it), pathological inputs (15M bare quotes, a 15M-space literal, 500k small literals) stay linear and fast, and the project suites test/write-boundary.mjs and test/sqlite-heap-execute.mjs pass, covering real DuckDB/SQLite round trips through installTrim.

findings.claim: The pairing test reads sql.charCodeAt(q + 1) === 39 and the trim test charCodeAt(end - 1) === 32; in a file whose comments otherwise explain every decision, the raw code points 39 (') and 32 (space) are the only unexplained magic numbers, and a future editor could easily 'fix' one of them wrongly.
